Service

Stop renting your own news.

Every release you publish on someone else's domain compounds someone else's authority. A branded newsroom puts the archive, the links and the rankings on your domain — where they keep working after the campaign ends.

Book a newsroom demoSee Studio plan
Quick answer A PressCosmos branded newsroom is a hosted, fully indexable press centre on your own domain. It publishes releases as NewsArticle-structured pages, hosts media assets and journalist resources, generates RSS and JSON feeds automatically, and keeps a permanent, searchable archive you control.

What is included

  • Custom domain with SSL and full visual branding
  • NewsArticle, Organization and BreadcrumbList structured data
  • Journalist resources: press contact, fact sheet, logo pack, executive bios
  • Multimedia galleries with automatic alt text and captions
  • Auto-generated RSS and JSON feeds for aggregators and partners
  • Category and tag archives that build topical authority
  • Search, date and category filtering for visitors
  • Revision history with visible correction notices
  • Localisation workflow for multi-language newsrooms
  • Analytics on the newsroom itself, not just the release

Why it compounds

A release published on a third-party wire earns a link once. The same release on your own newsroom, internally linked to the previous eighteen releases, becomes a topical cluster that search engines and retrieval systems read as evidence you are a consistent source on the subject.

Newsroom + distribution is the combination most comms teams should be running.

Setup

Live in a week

  1. 01

    Brand import

    We take your colours, type and logo and build the shell against your brand guide.

  2. 02

    Content migration

    Existing releases imported with original dates preserved for accurate archives.

  3. 03

    Domain and DNS

    Subdomain or root domain, SSL issued, redirects mapped from your old press page.

  4. 04

    Review and launch

    You approve on staging, we flip DNS and submit the sitemap.
